thesis: Temporal, AutoGen, AWS and Microsoft are commoditizing durable agent state and memory, so the uncommoditized asset remains a verified record that a delegated function closed work and how often it closed falsely; today's input is a fourth consecutive batch of template-scored 'operator runtime' signals (including one repo counted twice under two org names), which is live evidence that this loop itself has been proposing the same two fixes since 09-24 without a single shipped or killed receipt, and the deferred commercial hypothesis, that a buyer prices a governed function by its stated false-close rate before its harness, stays untested until Shadow has widened auto-close on its 20/20 audit and observed whether Will's review burden fell.
doctrine: A loop that has proposed the same artifact more than once without a shipped or killed receipt may not propose anything new; its only permitted output is the resolution of the prior proposal, and doing nothing is preferable to a fourth restatement.
proof_next_action: In the Shadow repository, run git log --since=2026-09-24 --oneline and grep the diff history for the auto-close expansion and the research-signal compiler dedupe; append one resolution entry per open proposal (09-24 compiler patch, 09-25 auto-close expansion) to the same ledger that stores frontier_compound_loop bets, each marked shipped with commit hash, killed with reason, or open with the concrete blocker, and commit that entry; no new proposal is emitted until both entries exist.
